Supported types are: [...] ## Indexing

By default, pgvector performs exact nearest neighbor search, which provides perfect recall.

You can add an index to use approximate nearest neighbor search, which trades some recall for speed. Unlike typical indexes, you will see different results for queries after adding an approximate index.

Supported index types are:

 HNSW
 IVFFlat

## HNSW [...] ```
SELECT FROM ORDER BY< ->'[3,1,2]' ' ' LIMIT 5
```

Supported distance functions are:

 `<->` - L2 distance
 `<#>` - (negative) inner product
 `<=>` - cosine distance
 `<+>` - L1 distance
 `<~>` - Hamming distance (binary vectors)
 `<%>` - Jaccard distance (binary vectors)

Get the nearest neighbors to a row

```
SELECT FROM WHERE!= 1 ORDER BY< -> SELECT FROM WHERE = 1 LIMIT 5
```

Get rows within a certain distance

```
SELECT FROM WHERE< ->'[3,1,2]' ' '< 5
```

results.content:
Title: pgvector/README.md at v0.3.1 · pgvector/pgvector · GitHub
## Navigation Menu. ## File metadata and controls. Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres. Supports L2 distance, inner product, and cosine distance. ## Installation. Compile and install the extension (supports Postgres 10+). Then load it in databases where you want to use it. You can also install it with Docker, Homebrew, or PGXN. Create a vector column with 3 dimensions. Get the nearest neighbor by L2 distance. Also supports inner product (`<#>`) and cosine distance (`<=>`). Note: `<#>` returns the negative inner product since Postgres only supports `ASC` order index scans on operators. Speed up queries with an approximate index. Add an index for each distance function you want to use. Indexes should be created after the table has some data for optimal clustering. Also, unlike typical indexes which only affect performance, you may see different results for queries after adding an approximate index. ### Index Options. Specify the number of inverted lists (100 by default). Specify the number of probes (1 by default). A higher value improves recall at the cost of speed. Use `SET LOCAL` inside a transaction to set it for a single query. Check indexing progress with Postgres 12+. Consider partial indexes for queries with a `WHERE` clause. To speed up queries without an index, increase `max_parallel_workers_per_gather`. To speed up queries with an index, increase the number of inverted lists (at the expense of recall). Each vector takes `4 * dimensions + 8` bytes of storage. Vectors can have up to 1024 dimensions. ### Vector Operators. | cosine\_distance(vector, vector) | cosine distance |. | inner\_product(vector, vector) | inner product |. | l2\_distance(vector, vector) | Euclidean distance |. | vector\_dims(vector) | number of dimensions |. | vector\_norm(vector) | Euclidean norm |. A non-partitioned table has a limit of 32 TB by default in Postgres. A partitioned table can have thousands of partitions of that size. ## Additional Installation Methods. Get the Docker image with:. This adds pgvector to the Postgres image. You can also build the image manually. With Homebrew Postgres, you can use:. Install from the PostgreSQL Extension Network with:. Install the latest version and run:. To get started with development:. ## Footer.

results.content:
Title: pgvector/README.md at v0.8.5 · pgvector/pgvector · GitHub
You signed in with another tab or window. You switched accounts on another tab or window. Open-source vector similarity search for Postgres. Store your vectors with the rest of your data. * exact and approximate nearest neighbor search. * single-precision, half-precision, binary, and sparse vectors. * L2 distance, inner product, cosine distance, L1 distance, Hamming distance, and Jaccard distance. * any language with a Postgres client. Plus ACID compliance, point-in-time recovery, JOINs, and all of the other great features of Postgres. Have a lot of vectors? ### Linux and Mac. Compile and install the extension (supports Postgres 13+). See the installation notes if you run into issues. You can also install it with Docker, Homebrew, PGXN, APT, Yum, pkg, APK, or conda-forge, and it comes preinstalled with Postgres.app and many hosted providers. You can also install it with Docker or conda-forge. Enable the extension (do this once in each database where you want to use it). Create a vector column with 3 dimensions. Also supports inner product (`<#>`), cosine distance (`<=>`), and L1 distance (`<+>`). Note: `<#>` returns the negative inner product since Postgres only supports `ASC` order index scans on operators. Create a new table with a vector column. Or add a vector column to an existing table. Also supports half-precision, binary, and sparse vectors. Get the nearest neighbors to a vector. Note: Combine with `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` to use an index. You can add an index to use approximate nearest neighbor search, which trades some recall for speed. Note: Use `halfvec_l2_ops` for `halfvec` and `sparsevec_l2_ops` for `sparsevec` (and similar with the other distance functions). You can also speed up index creation by increasing the number of parallel workers (2 by default). Note: Use `halfvec_l2_ops` for `halfvec` (and similar with the other distance functions). A higher value provides better recall at the cost of speed, and it can be set to the number of lists for exact nearest neighbor search (at which point the planner won’t use the index). Use the `halfvec` type to store half-precision vectors. You can use half-precision vectors or half-precision indexing to index up to 4,000 dimensions or binary quantization to index up to 64,000 dimensions.

Title: Support RabitQ in pgvector · Issue #1003 · pgvector/pgvector · GitHub
## Navigation Menu. You signed in with another tab or window. You switched accounts on another tab or window. ## Repository navigation. # Support RabitQ in pgvector #1003. opened on Jul 28, 2026. We have implemented RaBitQ quantization for both the IVFFlat and HNSW access method. on single heap table containing hundreds of millions of vectors. We would like to ask whether the maintainers are interested in accepting this work into pgvector. ## Benchmark. Our ann-benchmark results show that RaBitQ reduces index storage and improves. * After each index was built, `pg_prewarm` was used to load it into the PostgreSQL buffer cache before running search benchmarks. * `shared_buffers` was configured to be large enough to hold the indexes. This minimizes storage I/O during search and makes the benchmark focus on the distance-computation speedup provided by RaBitQ. + pgvector base version: v0.8.0. + ef\_search = 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180. ### IVFFlat. | Implementation | Build time | Index size |. | IVFFLAT baseline | 144.9s | 7820MB |. ### HNSW. | HNSW baseline | 359.76s | 7813MB |. If the maintainers are interested, we are willing to prepare the code for an. * Adding compatibility and fallback support for different CPU architectures. 1. ### ankanecommentedon Jul 28, 2026. I used this query to process benchmark with `dbpedia-openai-1000k-angular` dataset. ## Benchmark Configuration. Due to the large number of parameter combinations in the binary quantization experimental group, QPS-recall curves are used below. I think it'd also be good to try asymmetric binary quantization (quantize the indexed vectors but not the query vector) to see how it compares. the query vector remains an unquantized `vector` or `halfvec`. pgvector currently provides Hamming distance between two `bit` values, but it does not provide a distance operator between a binary-quantized vector and a vector. The index and query would conceptually look like this:. I think that this is a worthwhile comparison and would be happy to provide an implementation as a pull request. The performance gains look great, but the smaller indexes caught my eye just as much. Sign up for free **to join this conversation on GitHub.** Already have an account?

You switched accounts on another tab or window. ### Uh oh! There was an error while loading. * Notifications  You must be signed in to change notification settings. # Support for index rollout #840. ## Description. opened on May 19, 2025. Right now rolling out a new index can be fairly dangerous on production environments, especially for large indexes. ANN indexes need to be in memory to perform well, otherwise performance can drop substantially until the new index is brought to memory (as in, a couple of orders of magnitude). This can take several minutes if the index is large. If you are using partman this can be fixed by rolling one partition at a time, waiting some seconds for the new index to be brought to memory, then moving on to the next partition. Is there any similar approach being considered for pgvector? If not, do you think it would make sense for an extension to do this? Because if it does I think I might try to implement it. ## Metadata. ### Assignees. No fields configured for issues without a type. No branches or pull requests. ## Issue actions.
